question:
What fraction of $\mathrm{Fe}$ exists as $\mathrm{Fe}$ (III) in $\mathrm{Fe}_{0.96} \mathrm{O}$ ?
(Consider $\mathrm{Fe}_{0.96}$ to be made up of $\mathrm{Fe}$ (II) and $\mathrm{Fe}$ (III) only)
solution:
Let's assume $\mathrm{Fe}$ in $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}=\mathrm{x}$
Let's assume $\mathrm{Fe}$ in $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}(0.96-x)$
Using the charge conservation formula for
$\mathrm{Fe}_{0.96} \mathrm{O}_{1.00}$
We get: $(x)(+2)+(0.96-x)(+3)-2=0$
$\begin{aligned}
& =2 x+2.88-3 x-2=0 \\
& x=0.88
\end{aligned}$
So, number of ions of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}=0.96-x=0.96-0.88=0.08$
$\text {Fraction of } \mathrm{Fe}^{3+} \text { ion } =\frac{0.08}{0.96} =\frac{1}{12}$

question:
When electromagnetic radiation of wavelength $300 \mathrm{~nm}$ falls on the surface of a metal, electrons are emitted with the kinetic energy of $1.68 \times 10^5$ $\mathrm{J} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. What is the minimum energy needed to remove an electron from the metal?
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(h=6.626 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}, \mathrm{c}=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1},\right. \\
& \mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}}=6.022 \times 10^{23} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$

$h v=h v_0+\mathrm{KE}$
$h v_0=$ minimum energy required to remove electron)

$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{E}=\frac{h c}{\lambda} \\
& =\frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js} \times 3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}}{300 \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{~m}} \\
& =6.626 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~J}
\end{aligned}$
Energy of one mole of photons
$\begin{aligned}
& =6.626 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~J} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\
& =3.99 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$
The minimum energy needed to remove one mole of electrons $=(3.99-1.68) \times 10^5 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ $=2.31 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
